note: Every shipped asset, path and size, and where it came from. sw.js precaches exactly this list, so a card that adds a sprite adds it here and never to sw.js. assets/source/** is deliberately not listed: those are the unmodified pack archives, kept as provenance, and the start screen must not wait on a 22MB download. Terms live in ATTRIBUTION.md.
placement: A board square is 64 native px. Every piece sprite is a tight crop of the operator's own generated set with its alpha kept, box-downscaled to the size the game draws and quantised to one 32-colour palette; the game draws a piece at k = square/64 and stands it on the square, bottom-centred with its base on the square's bottom edge — the king lands 99 tall against the plastic pack's 102, so the scale the code has always used is unchanged. The two board squares are drawn, not cropped: flat 64x64 tiles in the set's own palette. The map's sprites are the same rule at a bigger size: the props, the markers and the beads are 2x exports of an SVG source beside the packs in assets/source/map/ (which is not precached), drawn at the size the map draws them — the drawn size is in each entry below — so a 64px stop is a 128px file. The world itself is not a sprite and is not a slice of anything: assets/map/world.png is the operator's own painting, cut to its own 640x272 pixel grid and drawn at a cover fit (src/map/terrain.js), so its pixels are magnified at every window shape. There is no SVG source for it, and no band cut from it: the three terrain bands and the 520px column they were cut for went with the world they composed.
